Question: A solid cube has side length \(3\) inches. A \(2\)-inch by \(2\)-inch square hole is cut into the center of each face. The edges of each cut are parallel to the edges of the cube, and each hole goes all the way through the cube. What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the remaining solid?
Solution:
Method 1: Subtract the newly removed volume

The holes from opposite faces trace the same tunnel, so there are three perpendicular tunnels. Each is a rectangular prism with volume
\[
2\cdot2\cdot3=12\text{ cubic inches}.
\]
Any two tunnels overlap in exactly the centered cube of side \(2\): their combined restrictions confine all three directions to the middle \(2\) inches. This overlap has volume \(2^3=8\), and it is the same central cube for every pair.

The first tunnel removes \(12\) cubic inches. Each later tunnel removes only \(12-8=4\) additional cubic inches, because its entire overlap with the earlier tunnels is that central cube. Therefore the remaining volume is
\[
3^3-12-4-4=27-20=7\text{ cubic inches}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

Method 2: Divide the remaining solid into boxes

Each centered \(2\)-inch opening leaves a margin of
\[
\frac{3-2}{2}=\frac12\text{ inch}
\]
on either side. Imagine slicing the cube along all the planes that form the sides of the tunnels. In each of the three directions, the resulting intervals have lengths \(\frac12,2,\frac12\).

A resulting box is removed whenever at least two of its intervals are middle \(2\)-inch intervals, since it then belongs to the tunnel running in the remaining direction. Thus a box survives exactly when it uses zero or one middle intervals.

With zero middle intervals, there are \(2^3=8\) corner cubes, each of side \(\frac12\). With one middle interval, there are \(3\) choices for its direction and \(2\) choices of outer interval in each other direction. This gives \(3\cdot2\cdot2=12\) prisms, each measuring \(2\) by \(\frac12\) by \(\frac12\).

These two cases exhaust the surviving boxes, whose interiors do not overlap. Their total volume is
\[
8\left(\frac12\right)^3+12\cdot2\left(\frac12\right)^2=1+6=7.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{7}\) cubic inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
